newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat steady ahead of EU tender result.
newsitem.headline: French wheat steady ahead of EU tender result.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Thursday after French exporters reduced their demands for wheat at this week's European Union grain auction, a further indication of a slow export scene, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen for January was quoted at 855-857.50 francs per tonne, unchanged from Wednesday.
In France exporters bid to ship 381,150 tonnes of EU wheat at rebates ranging from 11.90 to 18.95 Ecus per tonne.
Last week French exporters had placed demands for 576,000 tonnes.
Analysts said the lowest bid for a refund covered only 5,000 tonnes of exports while bids up top including 14.00 Ecus covered 25,000 tonnes of wheat.
"This is a rather slow week," one exporter said.
Wednesday's news that Iraq had bought between 250,000 and 275,000 tonnes of French wheat for March and April failed to stir prices as the move had been widely anticipated.
Tunisia bought a total of 125,000 tonnes of wheat on Thursday but it was still unclear if French wheat was included.
Matif fob barge French wheat futures were indicated at 881-886 francs per tonne but the market was untraded.
French cash grain prices exclude carrying charges of 3.64 francs per tonne which must be added to the quoted price for every half-month between August 1 last year and the delivery period in question.
